Class Experiment

java.lang.Object
com.eco.bio7.simulation.Experiment
public final class Experiment extends Object
Runs a model several times without a display (batch runs): a sweep of the parameters (all combinations of the given values), repetitions with other seeds and a number of steps. The runs are computed in parallel threads (one model for each run). The result is a table with a row for each recorded step of each run: the run, the seed, the values of the swept parameters, the step, the values of the line charts in this step (chart(...): the first chart by the name of the series, other charts as "chart: series") and the values of record(name, value). 
Experiment.Table t = new Experiment(SheepWolvesField.class)
                .param("growth", 0.02, 0.04, 0.06)
                .param("wolves", 4, 8, 12)
                .steps(500).repetitions(5).every(10)
                .run();
t.save("experiment.csv");   // a file of the project (relative path) or an absolute path
t.toR("experiment");        // a data frame in R (if R runs)
The seed of repetition k is seed + k (the same seeds for all parameter values: common random numbers). A run ends early if the model calls stop(). A model which sets its own seed in init() (seed(...)) gets the same numbers in all repetitions. Models with static fields which change should run in one thread (threads(1)).

    • design

      public Experiment design(String[] names, double[][] rows)
      Given parameter sets instead of (or combined with) the sweep, e.g. a Latin hypercube or the samples of a sensitivity analysis (created in R or Python): the names of the parameters and a row of values for each set. Each row is run with the repetitions; the column "point" of the table is the row of the design (0, 1, ...). Values of int fields are rounded. 
      new Experiment(NetworkEpidemic.class).design(new String[] { "infection", "recovery" },
                new double[][] { { 0.02, 0.04 }, { 0.05, 0.03 }, { 0.08, 0.06 } }).repetitions(5).run();
